_README: The SOURCE OF TRUTH for this agent's `capabilities.output_contract`.
A MIGRATION, not a new contract. This card was typed by hand before the
sketch compiler existed. The compiled output was diffed stamp-for-stamp
against the hand-written version before landing: 7 of 9 provenance stamps
byte-identical, no schema property added or removed, `required` unchanged,
grounding entries 0 -> 19. A migration that quietly narrowed a live agent's
stamps would be the recompile-narrowing bug this compiler already hit once
on `macro_data_agent`.
Two things came out of writing it, both landed first:
* `Coverage::PartialDeferred`, which did not exist. Every sourced block
here is `deferred` rather than `complete` -- the hand-written stamps all
admitted `pending_tool_check` and were right to, because the trace for a
real episode grades contracted fields `never asked` while the run made
seven other calls. `advanced_metrics` needed partial AND deferred; see
that block's `why`.
* `Compiled::merge_produces`. The compiler used to replace the card's
`produces`, and that column is also the port label set the seam census
matches on -- landing this would have deleted six labels, one of them
(`evidence`) named by eight other cards. Recorded as an open decision in
docs/plans/AGENT_COMPILE_AND_TOOL_REGISTRY.md section 6.8; the compile is
now additive.
Two stamps narrow ON PURPOSE. `ratings` and `squad_value` previously admitted
the human-settlement ladder (`human_sourced`, `human_endorsed`, ...) in their
DOCUMENT stamps, which let the AGENT record in its own output that a person
had verified an Elo it recalled from training data. Settlement is recorded in
`assertion_verifications` and read from there -- `assessment` is settled
`human_sourced` in production today while carrying a bare
`const: model_inference` stamp, which is the proof that the schema enum was
never what made settling work.
Read docs/guides/AGENT_CONTRACT_AUTHORING.md for the statuses.
title: Football evidence
description: Evidence supporting one driver of a Fermi forecast about a football fixture, league or competition. Every retrieved block comes from API-Football v3 through `call_football_api`; `assessment` is the agent's own judgement over them. The split is the product: three families of number this agent is asked for -- Elo ratings, squad market values, and Opta-style pressing metrics -- have no tool behind them at all, and the contract's job is to make a recalled Elo look different from a retrieved league position rather than letting them share a field.

calibration.note: A finished fixture's standings, statistics and head-to-head are immutable, so a replay settles them exactly and immediately. Injuries are a moving snapshot and a replay hours later legitimately disagrees; that block is scoreable only against a replay pinned to the original run's timestamp, which is why the delay is zero rather than a window.

blocks.name: league_context
blocks.description: Where the team sits in its league, and how it got there.

source.response_field: standings (rank, points, played, goals for/against, form string, home and away splits)

blocks.why: The `standings` endpoint returns position, points, played, goal difference and a form string directly, so nothing in this block needs inferring. `deferred` rather than `complete` because the agent is not obliged to call standings on every task -- a question about a single fixture's statistics need not fetch the table -- and a block that was never asked for must be able to say so instead of reporting `tool_no_match`, which would claim the endpoint was asked and had nothing.

blocks.name: fixtures
blocks.description: The schedule or results the analysis rests on.
blocks.why: The `fixtures` endpoint is the schedule, and rest days and congestion follow arithmetically from the dates it returns rather than from recall. Deferred for the same reason as `league_context`: a task about a finished match's head-to-head record does not need the fixture list, and an empty array must be distinguishable from an array that was never fetched.

blocks.name: head_to_head
blocks.description: The historical record between these two teams.
blocks.why: A dedicated endpoint takes `h2h: 'teamA-teamB'` and returns the record, so there is no reason for any of this to come from memory. Worth stating plainly because a fabricated historical record is both easy to produce and completely invisible to a reader -- nobody checks a claimed 3-1-2 over five meetings, and it reads exactly like a retrieved one.

blocks.name: injuries
blocks.description: The absences, as the tool reported them.
blocks.why: The `injuries` endpoint returns the roster of absences. The list is retrieved and the CONSEQUENCE of an absence is a judgement, so the estimated impact belongs in `assessment` and not here -- putting a modelled xG loss in the same block as a retrieved player name is precisely the mixing this contract exists to prevent. Deferred because the endpoint is frequently not called, and an empty injury list that was never fetched is a different claim from a squad with nobody injured.

blocks.name: match_statistics
blocks.description: What the match statistics endpoint reported for a specific fixture.

source.response_field: fixtures/statistics (shots on/off goal, shots in/out of box, blocked shots, possession, passes total and accurate, corners, offsides, fouls, cards, goalkeeper saves)

blocks.why: Every field here is on API-Football's documented statistics list and is retrievable per fixture, so all of it is a reading rather than an estimate. Deferred because the endpoint needs a fixture id: a question about a league table has no fixture to ask about, and the block is then legitimately unasked rather than empty.

blocks.name: advanced_metrics
blocks.description: Expected goals and the pressing metrics the card asks for, which are not all obtainable.
blocks.why: This block is split down the middle and the stamp has to say so. `xg` and `xga` ARE in fixture statistics -- an earlier draft of the field contract wrongly marked xG unsourced on the strength of the agent saying 'API-Football does not provide xG for these fixtures', which was true of the friendlies that episode looked at and false as a claim about the tool; trusting an agent's self-report about its own tool's coverage is the same error as trusting its self-report about a genome size. `xgd` is `xg - xga`, a subtraction that can be re-run. But `ppda`, `progressive_passes` and `set_piece_goal_share` are Opta and StatsBomb event-data metrics computed from defensive-action counts API-Football does not return, so they cannot be retrieved OR computed from what it does return. Hence both extra verdicts: `unavailable_no_tool_source` for the half that no call can ever fill, and `pending_tool_check` for the half that is obtainable but often not asked for. Dropping either would be a lie in a different direction.

blocks.name: ratings
blocks.description: Elo and Elo-derived probabilities. Nothing wired can supply these.

source.would_need: a ClubElo tool, or any Elo endpoint at all -- API-Football has none

blocks.why: The card's whole method section is built on Elo, and no tool this agent has returns one. An Elo it produces is therefore recalled from training data, and a stale Elo stated to four significant figures is indistinguishable from a measured one -- a previous run reported a precise rating while describing it as current. Declared unavailable so the value must be null and the absence is the contract being obeyed rather than a lookup that failed. Previously this block's stamp also admitted `human_sourced` and `human_endorsed`, which let the agent record in its own document that a person had verified a number the agent invented; settlement lives in `assertion_verifications` and is read from there, so removing them costs nothing and closes that.

blocks.name: squad_value
blocks.description: Market valuation and squad depth. Transfermarkt data, for which no tool exists.

source.would_need: a Transfermarkt or equivalent valuation feed

blocks.why: Market values and Big-5 league share come from Transfermarkt and there is no tool for it, so the agent has been supplying them from memory as factor X4 inputs. A market valuation out of training data is stale by construction and cannot be told apart from a current one by anybody reading the output. Same reasoning as `ratings`, including the removal of the human verdicts from the stamp: a person settling this claim is recorded in the verification queue, not asserted by the agent about itself.

blocks.name: assessment
blocks.description: The agent's own judgement over the retrieved blocks. This is the product.

source.from: the retrieved blocks above, weighed against the base rates in the agent's own card -- home win ~46%, draw ~26%, away ~28% across the top European leagues

blocks.why: This is what the agent is commissioned for and it must not be nulled: a contract that could not tell an agent which fabricates from one which reasons would have to delete this block, and would rightly be switched off for it. Stamped `model_inference` so a coordinator weighting several members' multipliers can see that this number was reasoned rather than read. The estimated impact of an injury belongs here rather than in `injuries` for the same reason.

blocks.name: summary
blocks.why: Permitted, and carries no provenance stamp because a retrieval verdict about a paragraph is a category error. It is not unchecked: `parse_evidence_text` lifts the summary out as the episode's evidence, so a fabrication survives there after every structured field has been cleared. An Elo or a market value recited in this paragraph is the same claim wearing a different hat, and the unsourced blocks above are what it gets checked against.
